findings.message: This migration is described as only adding the `data` column, but it also changes the primary key of all three tables (`ratelimitconfig`, `ratelimitcounter`, `ratelimitentry`) from AutoField to BigAutoField. On PostgreSQL and MySQL that rewrites each table and holds an exclusive lock for the whole rewrite. Rate-limit tables are hit on every request and can be large, so `migrate` can cause downtime or block traffic for a long time. Neither the CHANGELOG nor the upgrade notes mention it. Put the PK change in its own documented migration, or leave it out of this bug-fix release. The `data` AddField alone is enough to fix #24.

Whether the RenameIndex operations are included depends on which Django version runs the migration. The project still supports Django 3.2 and 4.0, which have no RenameIndex. On those versions the migration state keeps the old index names while the models expect the new ones. That leaves pending autodetected changes (`makemigrations --check` fails), and any later migration that refers to the new index names will break on those installs. A migration's operations should be the same on every version. Drop the cosmetic renames, or do them with a version-independent approach such as RemoveIndex/AddIndex, or with SeparateDatabaseAndState plus RunSQL.

A personal working checklist is committed to the repository root. It includes the author's local absolute paths (`/Users/yassershkeir/...`). It is not project documentation and should be removed from the change.

"apply the latest migration before upgrading" can't be followed, because the migration only arrives with the upgrade. It should say to run `migrate` after upgrading, before serving traffic. The entry also leaves out the BigAutoField PK changes and index renames included in the same migration.

`get()` now returns the JSON-decoded `data` whenever it is set, not `counter.count`. Values written through `set()` are first converted with `str()`, so their types change on the way back: `set(k, "123")` returns `get(k) == 123`, and `set(k, "true")` returns `True`. Token-bucket keys now return a dict instead of an int. Callers that relied on `get()` returning the count may break. Store values in a typed JSON envelope, or document the new behavior.

This bug fix has no regression tests. The PR's "I have added tests" box is unchecked, even though the committed checklist marks tests as added. Nothing tests that token-bucket state (fractional tokens, last_refill) persists across calls, that rows with `data` NULL from before the migration fall back correctly, or what `get()` now returns. Because `token_bucket_check` fails open on any exception, a regression here would quietly turn off rate limiting.

This bug-fix migration also changes the primary keys of all three tables from AutoField to BigAutoField. 0001_initial created them as AutoField. On PostgreSQL and MySQL this rewrites the whole table under an exclusive lock, and RateLimitEntry and RateLimitCounter can be large, busy tables. The PR describes only 'adding the data column' and claims backwards compatibility, so this downtime risk is unannounced. Split the PK change into its own documented migration, or leave it out of this patch.

Which operations run depends on the installed Django version. On Django 3.2 and 4.0, which pyproject still supports, the RenameIndex operations are skipped. The migration state then keeps the old index names, but the model Meta auto-generates the new ones. On those versions `migrate` warns about unreflected model changes, `makemigrations --check` fails in user projects, and running makemigrations creates a stray migration inside the installed package. The DB schema also differs between Django versions. Use version-independent operations (e.g. RunSQL/SeparateDatabaseAndState), or give the model indexes explicit names that match 0001.

If the new migration hasn't been applied, every token_bucket_check fails on the missing `data` column. The broad `except Exception` turns that into 'allow the request', so rate limiting is silently off with only an error log. The upgrade now depends on a migration, so this fail-open path deserves a louder signal (e.g. a system check for the column) rather than just README notes.

get() now returns deserialize_data(counter.data) without an expected type. Because set() stores scalars with str(), any string value that parses as JSON comes back as a different type: set('123') returns 123, set('true') returns True, set('null') returns None. The round-trip through set/get no longer preserves the value's type.

There are no tests for the new persistence behaviour: data round-trip, the fallback for old rows with data=NULL, initial_tokens capped at bucket_size, and the denied path persisting refilled tokens. The committed checklist says tests were added, but the diff has none, and the PR template leaves 'added tests' unchecked. This is the regression the PR fixes, so it should be covered.

A personal working checklist was committed to the repo root. It contains the author's absolute local filesystem paths (/Users/yassershkeir/...) and claims tests were added, which they weren't. Remove it from the change.

The changelog says 'apply the latest migration before upgrading', but the migration ships with the new version and can only run after upgrading. It should say to run `migrate` immediately after upgrading, and should mention the BigAutoField PK change and the index renames, which this migration also makes.

The docs say `showmigrations` will 'verify that the RateLimitCounter table now includes the `data` column'. It only lists which migrations are applied and doesn't inspect the schema, so the wording is misleading.
